study_identification_part.si_4_title: Distinct Neurodevelopmental Patterns and Intermediate Integration-Based Predictive Modeling in Autism Spectral Disorder

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: GAMLSS (Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape) was used to model developmental trajectories of brain morphology. The study used Sinh-Arcsinh (SHASH) distribution to estimate a four-parameter distribution (location, scale, skewness, kurtosis). Multiple model specifications were compared (M1a-M1e) with different combinations of age smooth effects and sex/site as fixed or random effects.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Generalized additive models for location, scale and shape (GAMLSS) can be used to model multi-parameter distributions, where each parameter of the distribution, i.e., location, scale, and shape, can be modeled as a function of several input variables, thereby accommodating a wide range of distributions [...] GAMLSS models were fitted to structural MRI data for the mean CT (MCT), total SA (TSA), and total GV (TGV) separately.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Wang2023.pdf.md: Methods / Modeling developmental trajectories of brain morphology (lines 53-67)

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Three cortical morphometric features were modeled: Mean Cortical Thickness (MCT), Total Surface Area (TSA), and Total Gray Matter Volume (TGV). These were extracted from FreeSurfer processing using the Desikan-Killiany atlas with 34 regions per hemisphere.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: GAMLSS models were fitted to structural MRI data for the mean CT (MCT), total SA (TSA), and total GV (TGV) separately. [...] For each participant, left and right cortical thickness (CT), surface area (SA), and gray matter volume (GV) measures were calculated.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Wang2023.pdf.md: Methods / Modeling developmental trajectories of brain morphology (line 61); Methods / MRI acquisition and preprocessing (lines 43-48)

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Multiple model specifications were tested with age as smooth effect for distribution parameters (mu, sigma, nu, tau), and sex and site as fixed or random effects. The best model (M1e) included age smooth effects and sex/site as random effects. Models were compared using AIC and BIC criteria.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: We can only choose model age smooth effect for mu and sigma (M1a), and add sex and site intercepts for mu and sigma as a fixed effect (M1b), and add age smooth effect for nu and tau (M1c), and add sex and site intercepts for nu and tau (M1d), and adjust sex and site for mu and sigma as random effects (M1e).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Wang2023.pdf.md: Methods / Modeling developmental trajectories of brain morphology (lines 61-67)
